what_it_is.prose: Skyroot Aerospace is a Hyderabad-based private launch vehicle startup founded in 2018 by former ISRO scientists Pawan Kumar Chandana (CEO) and Naga Bharath Daka (COO). Made history on 18 November 2022 with Vikram-S suborbital launch (Mission Prarambh) — India's first privately developed rocket to reach space. On 18 July 2026, Skyroot's Vikram-1 (4-stage orbital small-lift launch vehicle) made its maiden orbital flight (Mission Aagaman, Demo Flight) from Satish Dhawan Space Centre, becoming the first private Indian company to reach orbit. Vikram-1 places ~250 kg to 500 km LEO. Uses cryogenic upper stage and Kalam-series solid rocket motors — Kalam-5 test fired Dec 2020; Kalam-1200 (first stage of Vikram-1) first static test at SDSC-SHAR 8 Aug 2025; Kalam-250 (235 kN vacuum thrust, largest private Indian propulsion system) tested Mar 2024. Total funding $145M+; $1.1B valuation (May 2026 $60M round led by GIC + Sherpalo Ventures + BlackRock). Multi-launch deal signed with HEX20 (Aug 2026) for 3 dedicated Vikram missions from Q4 2027.

rows.platform_or_product: Vikram-S: suborbital all-carbon-composite rocket; first private Indian rocket to space (Mission Prarambh, 18 Nov 2022)
Vikram-1: 4-stage expendable orbital small-lift launch vehicle; first private Indian rocket to orbit (Mission Aagaman demo flight, 18 July 2026); ~250 kg to 500 km LEO
Vikram-2 / Vikram-3: planned higher-capacity variants in development
Kalam series solid rocket motors: Kalam-5 (test fired Dec 2020), Kalam-250 (235 kN vacuum thrust
rows.india_status: largest private Indian propulsion system, tested Mar 2024), Kalam-1200 (first-stage booster of Vikram-1, first static test at SDSC-SHAR 8 Aug 2025)

rows.context: Vikram-S Mission Prarambh — successful suborbital launch from Sriharikota on 18 November 2022 at 11:30 IST; India's first privately developed rocket to space

Vikram-1 Mission Aagaman (Demo Flight) — first orbital launch 18 July 2026 at 06:35 UTC from First Launch Pad, SDSC-SHAR; first private Indian company to reach orbit (delayed from original Sept 2025 target)
Kalam-5 solid propulsion rocket stage successfully test-fired 28 December 2020
Kalam-250 engine successfully tested (235 kN vacuum thrust — largest propulsion system in India's private space sector) — March 2024
First static test of KALAM 1200 solid motor at SDSC-SHAR — 8 August 2025 (Vikram-1 first-stage booster)
Multi-launch agreement with HEX20 (signed Aug 2026) for 3 dedicated Vikram missions from Q4 2027 to deploy EO and demo satellites
Series C-equivalent $60M funding round (May 2026) led by GIC + Sherpalo Ventures + BlackRock → $1.1B valuation; total capital ~$145-160M

faq.question: When did Skyroot launch Vikram-1 and what was the significance?
faq.answer: 18 July 2026 (Mission Aagaman demo flight) from SDSC-SHAR — Skyroot became the first private Indian company to reach orbit

faq.question: What was India's first privately developed rocket?
faq.answer: Skyroot's Vikram-S, launched 18 November 2022 (Mission Prarambh) — a suborbital flight from Sriharikota

faq.question: What is the Kalam-1200?
faq.answer: The first-stage solid motor booster for Skyroot's Vikram-1 launch vehicle — first static test conducted at SDSC-SHAR on 8 August 2025

faq.question: What is Skyroot's current valuation?
faq.answer: $1.1 billion (unicorn status), achieved May 2026 after $60M funding round led by GIC, Sherpalo Ventures and BlackRock; total raised ~$145M
